findings.claim: The q3 rationale's shape claim about 'inference' is false: 'interference' is the shape-closest distractor to the key 'indifference', not 'inference'.
findings.evidence: q3 rationale (candidates-final): "inference = sense misfit: it is a term for a step in reasoning and has no bearing on what makes a small favour easy to ask, though its shape sits closest of all to the key." Measured against key 'indifference' (12 letters, 4 syllables): 'interference' = 12 letters, 4 syllables, Levenshtein 3, shares the in-…-ference frame exactly; 'inference' = 9 letters, 3 syllables, Levenshtein 3. On length and syllable count 'interference' is strictly closer; on edit distance it ties. No metric makes 'inference' 'closest of all'.
findings.why: The rationale is the teaching payload a student reads after answering. A student who picked 'interference' is told the option they chose is shape-distant while a shorter option is 'closest of all' — a checkable, wrong claim in the explanation. It does not touch the key (the trap label 'sense misfit' is correct and 'indifference' remains the single defensible answer), so it is a rationale-precision defect rather than an item defect, and it does not overturn the recorded MINOR_FIXES verdict.

findings.claim: A residual passage-level tension survives at the gap-(4) sentence: the paragraph asserts outcomes are unknowable and then, unhedged, asserts an outcome.
findings.evidence: Passage: "None of it can be checked. Nobody writes down what was asked for, and nobody writes down what came of it, so there is no telling whether the ladder was ever lent. Most of what goes up ___(4)___ to nothing." With the key 'comes', the third sentence states a fact about outcomes immediately after the second denies that any such fact can be had, and it carries no hedge ('probably', 'no doubt'). The pedagogy pass demonstrably noticed the problem — the q4 rationale was changed from "it follows directly from the sentence before it" (candidates-corrected) to "it is the columnist's own concession about the board's traffic, picking up the 'what came of it' of the sentence before" (candidates-final) — but the fix reframed the rationale and left the passage sentence untouched.
findings.why: Reported as an observation, not a refutation. Re-labelling the sentence a 'concession' is a defensible essayistic reading, and the gap is a pure collocation gap ('come to nothing' is the only idiomatic option among comes/carries/cuts/counts), so neither the key nor its defensibility is affected. It is exactly the class of residue MINOR_NOTES describes, so the recorded integrated verdict stands.

audit_scope_notes.language: Hunted the passage and all 20 options for calque, agreement, register and spelling-variety defects; found none that would move the CORRECTED verdict. BrE is held throughout ('noticeboard', 'metre', 'fortnight', 'guttering', 'neighbourliness', 'churchyard', 'going spare', 'is lucky to see a fortnight', 'live next door to'); no AmE-only form and no -ize spelling appears in passage, prompts or options. Typography scan of the shipping file: 20 en dashes (U+2013), 0 em dashes, 9 curly apostrophes (U+2019), 0 straight apostrophes — the batch15 addendum dash rule holds. Locative inversion agrees ('on the ledge beside it stands a jam jar'); the earlier relative-clause misattachment ('on the ledge beside it that anyone may use') was already repaired by the language pass. 'tenors wanted, urgently, by a choir that has four' is an elliptical joke whose antecedent is arguably 'members' rather than 'tenors', but the repair is one a native reader makes without effort and it is not gap-bearing.
audit_scope_notes.pedagogy: Fact-checked every factual claim in all five rationales. The idiom claims hold: 'spare someone's feelings' (not 'save'), 'give/get short shrift', 'count FOR nothing', 'carry weight' / 'carry the day', 'cut to the chase' / 'cut to the bone', 'catch someone's drift' / 'snow drift'. The POS-uniformity claims hold (s- verbs at 1, -ift nouns at 2, -ference nouns at 3, c- verbs at 4, formal connective adverbs at 5). The gap-5 logic analysis is sound: an indefensible arrangement is a reason to replace it, so 'Accordingly' reverses the arrow. The only false claim found is the shape claim recorded above.
audit_scope_notes.integrated: Every quoted phrase in every rationale was checked against the current passage and option text and all appear verbatim, including the en dash inside 'indefensible on ordinary grounds – unaccountable, unmeasured, and administered by one man with a jam jar', plus 'has not been refused', 'has only gone unread', 'what came of it', 'still go up as they always have' and the four gap frames. No rationale contradicts itself. No cross-question leak: no gap's answer is recoverable from another gap's context or rationale. Trap labels name the actual trap in all cases (collocation_misfit at 1/2/4, polarity_mirror for 'deference' at 3, wrong_logic at 5). Metadata reconciles with content: key_letters 'C / A / D / B / C' matches the keyed answers, all four letters are used with no column, 5 gaps map to 5 questions[], prompts are 2 tokens and every option is 1 token, gap_type_map and gap_pos_map match the items, the title is the claimed flat two-word noun phrase, and the internal date arithmetic holds ('stopped teaching in 2014' against 'more than a decade of first Mondays' at a 2026 present). No name in the unit ('Verity Padgham', 'Wilf Braddick', 'Denhollow') collides with the BRIEF-ADDENDUM name registry, the institutions/publications list, or the 93-family exclusion list.
audit_scope_notes.key_sanity: All five keys are the single best answer and defensible to a complaining student. (1) 'spares' — the only verb that collocates with 'feelings'; 'saves nobody's feelings' is the strongest lure and is not English. (2) 'shrift' — fixed idiom; 'short shift' is the classic misform. (3) 'indifference' — the only option that opposes 'neighbourliness' and is cashed out by 'has not been refused. It has only gone unread'. (4) 'comes' — 'count FOR nothing' takes the wrong preposition against the frame's 'to'. (5) 'Nonetheless' — the only concessive against 'indefensible on ordinary grounds'. The one apparent counterexample to gap 1's reading, the piano card left up to avoid making 'a statement', is flagged by the passage itself as 'The exception' and so does not undercut the key.
